n: After hearing Isaiah, Nephi’s brothers ask a sincere question: are these prophecies only spiritual, or will they happen literally? It is a sign of progress that they ask at all.
Nephi explains that the Spirit revealed these things to Isaiah, and the Spirit shows prophets what will actually happen to people “according to the flesh” — that is, in real life.

f.w: by the Spirit are all things made known

n: The prophecies are both temporal and spiritual. Israel will literally be scattered across the earth among every nation.

f.w: scattered upon all the face of the earth

n: Many Israelites are already lost to those at Jerusalem — most of the tribes were taken away (by Assyria, about 722 BC) and scattered. No one knows exactly where they went. These are often called the lost ten tribes.

f.w: the more part of all the tribes have been led away

n: The prophecies apply to these lost tribes and to all who will later be scattered for hardening their hearts against the Holy One of Israel. They will be hated among the nations.
Nephi interprets Isaiah 49:22–23: the Gentiles nursing Israel and carrying her children are literal, temporal events. They apply to Lehi’s descendants and all Israel in the future.
After Israel is scattered, God will raise a mighty Gentile nation in this very land — the Americas — and that nation will scatter Lehi’s descendants. Many see this as the United States.

f.w: a mighty nation among the Gentiles

n: Then God will do a “marvelous work” among the Gentiles that will greatly bless Lehi’s descendants — the restoration of the gospel and the coming forth of the Book of Mormon. This is how the Gentiles “carry” Israel.
This work will bless Gentiles and all Israel, revealing the covenants made to Abraham that through his seed all the earth would be blessed.

f.w: In thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed

n: The world can only be blessed if God “makes bare His arm” — rolls up His sleeve, so to speak, and shows His power openly.

f.g: Roll back the sleeve to act with full strength.

n: God will show His power to all nations by bringing His covenants and gospel to Israel.

f.w: in the eyes of all the nations

n: Israel will be freed from captivity, gathered to their promised lands, brought out of spiritual darkness, and will know the Lord as their Savior and Redeemer.

f.w: out of obscurity and out of darkness

n: Nephi explains Isaiah 49:26: the great and abominable church will turn on itself; its violence will come back on its own head.
Nations that fight Israel will turn on each other and fall into the pit they dug for God’s people. All who fight Zion will be destroyed, and the great and abominable church will collapse.

Satan will soon lose his power over people’s hearts. The proud and wicked will be like stubble that is burned — dry leftover stalks, quickly consumed. Nephi quotes a prophet whose words also appear later in Malachi.

f.g: The dry stalks left after harvest.

n: God’s full wrath will be poured out on the wicked, because He will not allow them to destroy the righteous.

f.w: fulness of the wrath of God

n: Even if fire must destroy their enemies, God will preserve the righteous by His power. The righteous need not fear: they will be saved, “even as by fire.”

f.w: saved, even if it so be as by fire

n: Blood, fire, and smoke will come upon the earth for those who harden their hearts against the Holy One of Israel.

f.w: blood, and fire, and vapor of smoke

n: The righteous will not perish, but all who fight against Zion will be cut off.
Nephi cites Moses’ prophecy that God would raise up a prophet like Moses; whoever refuses to hear Him will be cut off.

f.w: A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you, like unto me

n: Nephi identifies that prophet: the Holy One of Israel — Jesus Christ — who will judge in righteousness. The New Testament and Christ Himself (in 3 Nephi) say the same.

f.w: this prophet of whom Moses spake was the Holy One of Israel

n: The righteous need not fear and will not be put to shame. It is the devil’s kingdom, established among mortals, that is in danger.

Nephi describes the kingdom of the devil: churches built for money, power, or popularity; and all who seek fleshly lusts, worldly things, and iniquity. They are the ones who should tremble — they will be consumed like stubble.

f.w: popular in the eyes of the world

n: The righteous will be led up like calves from the stall — well fed and leaping with joy — and the Holy One of Israel will reign in glory.

f.g: Calves kept and fed in a barn; once released they leap for joy.

n: The Good Shepherd gathers His children from every corner of the earth. His sheep know Him, and there will be one fold and one shepherd.
Because His people are righteous, Satan will have no power and will be bound for many years — the Millennium. Satan is bound because the people’s own righteousness gives him no place in their hearts.

f.w: he cannot be loosed for the space of many years

n: Nephi repeats: all these things will literally happen.
Every nation and people can be safe in the Holy One of Israel — if they repent. The invitation is universal.

f.w: if it so be that they will repent

n: Nephi stops here; he does not yet dare say more about these things.
Nephi asks his brothers to consider that the brass plates are true and teach that a person must obey God’s commandments.

Lehi and Nephi are not the only witnesses — many prophets have taught the same. Nephi ends the first book with a simple promise: keep the commandments and endure to the end, and you will be saved at the last day.
